newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chip slump hits Hitachi, Mitsubishi's group profit.
newsitem.headline: Chip slump hits Hitachi, Mitsubishi's group profit.

text.p: Japanese chip makers Mitsubishi Electric Corp and Hitachi Ltd saw their profits nosedive in the first half of the business year as sluggish demand for personal computers adversely affected chip prices.
While tumbling chip prices dented earnings of most electronics makers, the two were particularly hurt by weaker demand for personal computers -- which use a large amount of memory chips.
"We strongly feel a need to strengthen our PC business," said a Mitsubishi Electric spokesman.
The companies, which do not make PCs like their bigger Japanese counterparts, said sluggish consumer appliance sales hurt their efforts to recoup losses from lower chip prices.
Mitsubishi Electric said its group net profit dropped a sharp 75 percent to 6.3 billion yen ($55.7 million) for the April-September period from the year-earlier period.

Amid a supply glut following a worldwide slowdown in PC sales, prices of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) -- the current mainstay products used in PCs -- fell more than 70 percent from earlier this year.
With a sharp recovery in prices unlikely soon, Mitsubishi said it has revised down the value of its semiconductor production target for the year to end-March 1997 to 500 billion yen ($4.42 billion).
The company produced 550 billion yen ($4.86 billion) worth of chips in the 1995/96 business year.
At Hitachi, interim group profits fell 42 percent to 33.6 billion yen ($297 million) for the six months, from 57.7 billion yen ($510 million) in the year-earlier period.
"Despite higher profits in the electric power and industrial system division, group net profits plunged due to the negative impact of lower chip prices," Hitachi said.
The bright spot was losses at its troubled consumer electrical appliance division narrowed, helped in part by strong sales of air conditioners, an Hitachi spokeswoman said.
Hitachi forecast group profits to fall by 44 percent in the full year to 80 billion yen ($707 million), while Mitsubishi expects a 58 percent drop to 25 billion yen ($221 million).
Despite sagging chip prices, diversified product lines kept some other makers, like NEC Corp, profitable as a spicier mix of products softened the blow from the downturn in the chip market.

NEC, Japan's biggest chip maker, earlier reported a 54 percent jump in group net profit to 31.21 billion yen ($276 million) as buoyant sales of telecommunications equipment more than compensated for lower chip prices.
Another major electronics firm Toshiba Corp will announce its group half-year results and full-year forecast on Friday.
Analysts expect any fall in Toshiba's group net profits to be limited due to the strength of its PC business.
